12. Unusual Characteristics of the Section 4(f) Land:
There are no significantly unusual or unique characteristics associated with the Section 4(f) Land.
13. Consistency of Location, Type of Activity, and Use of the Section 4(f) Land with Community Goals, Objectives, and Land Use Planning
The Woodrow Wilson Woods of the Thorn Creek Division of the Cook County Forest Preserve District is consistent with the land use plans present and proposed, of the City of Chicago Heights as well as open space plans of Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission. There have been no known inconsistences expressed by the surrounding communities, Olympia Fields, Park Forest and Matteson concerning community goals, objectives, and land use planning. See Exhibit "F" The Land Use map for the 4(f) Lands.
The Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission A-95 review, dated May 22, 1974 for the improvement of Lincoln Highway from Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road in Cook County states:
"The project is found to be consistent with regional planning policies as set forth in the Comprehensive General Plan and with currently adopted Commission Plans and programs."
The Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission (Metro-politan Clearinghouse) A-95 review dated May 22, 1974, the Interstate Planning Committee review dated May 22, 1974, and the Illinois State Clearinghouse review dated July 24, 1975 are contained in Appendix D.
14. Prior Use of State or Federal Funds for Acquisition or Development of the Section 4(f) Land
The acquisition, funding, and development of the Section 4(f) Land was done by the Cook County Forest Preserve District. There has been no prior use of State or Federal Funds for the acquisition or development of the Section 4(f) Land.
